p: Escape rooms can be a bit of a shock to the system first time round. There's no instruction manual, no obvious starting point, and the clock is ticking. The trick is to get the whole team searching straight away. Open everything you can, look under, behind and inside, and pile up anything that seems useful in one spot. Once you've got your stash, start linking things together. Codes, keys and clues nearly always connect to something else in the room.

Leeds is a big student city, and escape rooms are a favourite for freshers' socials and end-of-term celebrations. They're just as popular with families and office teams, as no one needs any special skills to join in. For bigger groups, booking side-by-side rooms and racing each other is a cracking way to up the stakes. Take a team photo at the end, win or lose, because the faces tell the whole story.

The Light is close to Millennium Square, which puts plenty of culture within a few minutes' walk. Leeds City Museum sits right on the square and is free to explore, with everything from ancient worlds to local history. The grand Victorian Leeds Town Hall and Leeds Art Gallery are close by on The Headrow, with the Henry Moore Institute next door for sculpture fans. Theatre lovers can take their pick of the Grand Theatre or Leeds Playhouse. A bit further out, the Royal Armouries at Leeds Dock showcases centuries of arms and armour, and Roundhay Park, a huge green space in the north of the city, offers lakes, gardens and woodland walks when you want some fresh air.
